ov_en: Spring Cloud is a core microservices framework; its vulnerabilities can affect an entire microservice cluster. Known critical CVEs include Spring Cloud Gateway SpEL injection (CVE-2022-22947) and Spring Cloud Function RCE (CVE-2022-22963).
vu_en: Spring Cloud vulnerabilities: 1) Gateway Actuator SpEL injection via /actuator/gateway/routes 2) Cloud Function SpEL injection via spring.cloud.function.routing-expression header 3) Config Server path traversal to read arbitrary files.
ex_en:
1. Identify Spring Cloud components
2. Detect exposed Actuator endpoints
3. Exploit known CVEs
4. Execute commands or read files
mi_en: Upgrade to patched versions, disable unnecessary Actuator endpoints, enforce access controls, monitor for anomalous requests.

ov_en: Apache Struts2 has a long history of RCE vulnerabilities (S2-001 through S2-066+) rooted in OGNL expression injection. Struts2 flaws caused major breaches (e.g., Equifax) and remain prime attacker targets.
vu_en: Struts2 RCE exploits OGNL expression injection: %{expression} or ${expression} in user input is evaluated as OGNL, executing Java code. High-severity CVEs include S2-045 (Content-Type header), S2-046 (filename), and S2-057 (namespace).
ex_en:
1. Identify Struts2 framework
2. Detect vulnerable version
3. Select applicable CVE exploit
4. Execute commands or obtain reverse shell
mi_en: Upgrade to latest version, disable dynamic method invocation, strictly filter user input, deploy WAF.

ov_en: OGNL is Struts2's core expression language, providing powerful access to the Java object graph. OGNL injection can create ProcessBuilder/Runtime objects to execute OS commands—the root cause of the vast majority of Struts2 RCE vulnerabilities.
vu_en: OGNL injection methods: 1) Modify security manager config via #_memberAccess 2) Execute commands via @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec() 3) Use ProcessBuilder 4) Load remote malicious classes via ClassLoader 5) Evolving OGNL sandbox bypass techniques per Struts2 version.
ex_en:
1. Understand OGNL syntax
2. Bypass security restrictions
3. Execute OS commands
4. Retrieve command output
mi_en: Upgrade Struts2, strictly filter user input, disable OGNL expressions, configure security restrictions.

ov_en: Oracle WebLogic Server is an enterprise Java application server with recurring T3/IIOP deserialization, SSRF, and RCE vulnerabilities. WebLogic flaws typically yield direct server compromise and are top-priority Java environment targets.
vu_en: WebLogic critical CVEs: 1) T3 deserialization (CVE-2015-4852/CVE-2018-2628) 2) XMLDecoder deserialization (CVE-2017-10271) 3) SSRF (CVE-2014-4210 accessing internal Redis) 4) Unauthenticated console access 5) IIOP deserialization. Oracle CPU patches new WebLogic flaws quarterly.
ex_en:
1. Identify WebLogic version
2. Probe open ports and endpoints
3. Select applicable CVE exploit
4. Execute commands or write WebShell
mi_en: Apply Oracle Critical Patch Updates promptly, close unnecessary T3/IIOP ports, restrict management console access by IP, deploy WAF, use network segmentation, monitor for anomalous class loading.

ov_en: WebLogic T3 is its proprietary RMI communication protocol used for cluster communication and JNDI lookups. T3 deserialization vulnerabilities allow remote attackers to send malicious serialized objects and execute arbitrary code.
vu_en: T3 deserialization exploit chain: establish a T3 handshake, then send serialized data containing a malicious gadget chain (e.g., Commons Collections). Tools like ysoserial generate payloads; T3Exploit/WebLogic-T3-RCE automate exploitation. WebLogic blacklist filters can be bypassed with new gadgets.
ex_en:
1. Probe T3 port
2. Confirm WebLogic version
3. Select gadget chain
4. Send malicious serialized object
5. Execute commands
mi_en: Disable T3 or restrict access, apply latest patches, use network firewall, monitor for anomalous serialization requests.

ov_en: WebLogic IIOP (Internet Inter-ORB Protocol) is a CORBA standard communication protocol that also has deserialization vulnerabilities. When T3 is blocked by a firewall, the IIOP port (default 7001) serves as an alternative RCE entry point.
vu_en: IIOP deserialization is conceptually similar to T3 but uses CORBA protocol encapsulation, bypassing T3 blacklist filters due to different deserialization code paths. CVE-2020-2551 achieves RCE via the IIOP protocol.
ex_en:
1. Probe IIOP port
2. Use CVE-2020-2551 exploit tool
3. Send malicious serialized object
4. Execute commands
mi_en: Disable IIOP if unused, restrict IIOP network access to trusted cluster nodes only, apply Oracle security patches promptly, deploy RASP to detect malicious class loading.

ov_en: ThinkPHP is the most popular PHP framework in China, with multiple RCE vulnerabilities in historical versions (3.x/5.x/6.x). Its widespread use in Chinese government, education, and e-commerce makes it a high-value mass-exploitation target.
vu_en: ThinkPHP critical vulnerabilities: 1) 5.0.x route parameter RCE (invoke arbitrary methods via controller/action injection) 2) 5.1.x Request class method override RCE 3) 5.x multi-language module file inclusion 4) 3.x cache file write GetShell 5) 6.x deserialization POP chain. Exploit URL: /index.php?s=/index/think\app/invokefunction.
ex_en:
1. Identify ThinkPHP version
2. Select applicable exploit method
3. Execute commands or write shell
4. Obtain server access
mi_en: Upgrade to latest patched version, disable DEBUG mode and error display, configure strict routing mode, remove unnecessary entry files and modules, deploy WAF rules for ThinkPHP signature payloads.

ov_en: Laravel is PHP's most popular modern framework. Its RCE vulnerabilities primarily stem from deserialization POP chains, Debug mode information disclosure (Ignition component), and insecure configuration (APP_KEY leakage enabling encrypted cookie forgery).
vu_en: Laravel vulnerabilities: 1) Ignition RCE (CVE-2021-3129: log clear + phar deserialization) 2) Cookie deserialization (forge encrypted cookies after APP_KEY leakage to trigger POP chain) 3) Debug mode leaks DB passwords/API keys 4) Blade template injection ({!!$input!!} unescaped).
ex_en:
1. Detect Laravel version and components
2. Attempt .env file disclosure
3. Exploit Ignition RCE, or
4. Forge identity using leaked APP_KEY
mi_en: Disable debug mode, upgrade Ignition component, protect .env file, rotate APP_KEY regularly.

ov_en: Apache Shiro's RememberMe feature uses AES-encrypted serialized objects; a hardcoded default key leads to a deserialization RCE vulnerability.
vu_en: Shiro RememberMe Cookie uses AES-CBC encryption (default key: kPH+bIxk5D2deZiIxcaaaA==). Attack flow: 1) Detect fingerprint (rememberMe=deleteMe in response) 2) Use default key or brute-force key 3) Generate gadget chain with ysoserial 4) AES-encrypt + Base64-encode as Cookie value.
ex_en:
1. Detect Shiro framework
2. Obtain or brute-force the key
3. Generate malicious serialized object
4. AES-encrypt and send as Cookie
5. Trigger deserialization to execute commands
mi_en: Replace default key, upgrade Shiro version, use a secure serialization mechanism, monitor for anomalous Cookie patterns.

ov_en: JBoss (now WildFly) is Red Hat's Java application server with numerous historical critical vulnerabilities: JMXInvokerServlet deserialization, unauthenticated JBoss console WAR deployment, and EJBInvokerServlet remote invocation—a high-risk asset in internal Java environments.
vu_en: JBoss critical vulnerabilities: 1) JMXInvokerServlet deserialization (CVE-2015-7501) 2) /jmx-console/ unauthenticated access for WAR backdoor deployment 3) /invoker/JMXInvokerServlet remote method invocation 4) EJBInvokerServlet deserialization 5) JBoss Seam parameter injection (CVE-2010-1871) 6) Management console weak credentials (admin:admin).
ex_en:
1. Scan for JBoss service
2. Probe exposed endpoints
3. Exploit deserialization or deploy WAR
4. Obtain server access
mi_en: Remove unnecessary endpoints, enforce access controls, upgrade JBoss version, network isolation.

ov_en: Apache Tomcat is the most widely used Java Servlet container. Common vulnerabilities include AJP file read/inclusion (GhostCat), PUT method file write, and Manager WAR backdoor deployment. Manager application weak credentials (tomcat:tomcat) are the most common intrusion entry point.
vu_en: Tomcat critical vulnerabilities: 1) AJP file read/inclusion (CVE-2020-1938 GhostCat) 2) PUT method file write (CVE-2017-12615) 3) Manager weak credentials for WAR WebShell deployment 4) Session deserialization (FileStore persistence) 5) JSP execution path traversal (CVE-2020-9484) 6) Default page information disclosure.
ex_en:
1. Scan for Tomcat service
2. Attempt weak credential login
3. Deploy malicious WAR package, or
4. Exploit applicable CVE
mi_en: Change default credentials, restrict Manager access by IP, disable AJP or configure a secret, upgrade Tomcat version.

ov_en: Django is Python's most mature web framework with strong security defaults, but vulnerabilities still exist: SQL injection (JSONField/Raw SQL), debug mode information disclosure, CSRF token bypass, and template injection in custom tags.
vu_en: Django vulnerabilities: 1) DEBUG=True leaks full config, DB info, and source paths 2) JSONField/HStoreField SQL injection (CVE-2019-14234) 3) Truncation attack (email address truncation bypass) 4) StringAgg SQL injection 5) URL validation bypass (is_valid_url) 6) Password reset token prediction.
ex_en:
1. Detect Django version
2. Exploit debug mode to gather information
3. Exploit SQL injection, or
4. Forge identity using leaked SECRET_KEY
mi_en: Disable debug mode, upgrade Django version, protect SECRET_KEY, input validation.

ov_en: Flask is a lightweight Python web framework. Its security vulnerabilities primarily stem from developer mistakes: Secret Key leakage leading to session forgery, Jinja2 SSTI, Debug mode RCE (Werkzeug debugger), and insecure deserialization.
vu_en: Flask security risks: 1) Werkzeug debugger in debug mode executes arbitrary Python (requires PIN, but PIN is calculable via file reads) 2) Secret Key leakage enables session cookie forgery 3) Jinja2 template injection (render_template_string) 4) Insecure pickle session serialization.
ex_en:
1. Detect Flask framework
2. Test SSTI injection
3. Exploit debug mode, or
4. Forge session
mi_en: Disable debug mode, protect SECRET_KEY, filter template injection, input validation.

ov_en: SQL injection WAF bypass techniques circumvent web application firewall protections via encoding obfuscation, chunked transfer, inline comments, case variation, and equivalent function substitution—achieving data extraction and access even in WAF-protected environments.
vu_en: WAFs rely on regex matching and keyword detection but cannot cover all encoding variants and syntax mutations. Attackers exploit parsing differences between the database engine and the WAF parser to craft statements the WAF cannot recognize but the database executes normally.
ex_en: Identify WAF type/version via response headers and block pages, then systematically test bypass techniques: double URL encoding, Unicode encoding, inline comment keyword splitting (/*!50000SELECT*/), equivalent function substitution (MID instead of SUBSTR), HTTP parameter pollution, and chunked transfer encoding.
mi_en: Use parameterized queries to eliminate SQL injection at the root; treat WAF as a defense-in-depth layer only. Regularly update WAF rule sets, enable deep decoding (recursive URL/Unicode decode), apply rate limiting and behavioral analysis on anomalous requests, and combine with RASP for runtime detection.

ov_en: Authentication bypass covers multiple techniques that skip identity verification mechanisms—default credentials, logic flaws, session fixation, response manipulation, forced browsing—directly obtaining unauthorized system access. One of the most prevalent high-severity web vulnerabilities.
vu_en: Authentication implementation flaws include: hardcoded default credentials never forced to change, authentication state determined solely by client-side parameters, password reset flow logic vulnerabilities, predictable session token generation, multi-step authentication flow skippable, and improper OAuth/SAML implementations enabling identity spoofing.
ex_en: Enumerate authentication endpoints and flows, test default credentials (admin/admin, etc.), analyze status codes and parameters in authentication responses, attempt modifying authentication flags (false→true), test direct access to post-auth pages (forced browsing), verify JWT signature validation strictness, test concurrent logins and race conditions.
mi_en: Implement MFA; disable all default credentials and force password change on first login; perform authentication state checks server-side only; use cryptographically secure random session tokens; enforce server-side access control on all protected resources; implement account lockout and anomalous login alerting.

ov_en: File upload bypass techniques circumvent web application upload protections via extension manipulation, MIME type spoofing, content-type confusion, double extensions, null bytes, and image polyglots—ultimately uploading executable malicious files (WebShells) to gain server control.
vu_en: File upload validation flaws: client-only JavaScript validation, checking only Content-Type header without inspecting actual content, incomplete blacklists (missing php5/phtml/phar variants), no file renaming or isolated storage, executable permissions in upload directory, no magic byte verification, and parsing vulnerabilities executing non-standard extensions.
ex_en: Test normal upload flow to identify allowed types, then attempt: changing Content-Type to image/jpeg, double extension (test.php.jpg), null byte truncation (test.php%00.jpg), Windows alternate data stream (test.php::$DATA), case variants (test.PhP), .htaccess override, and image polyglot (appending PHP code to legitimate image). Verify parsed execution after successful upload.
mi_en: Server-side file type validation using magic bytes (not extension); rename uploaded files (UUID); disable script execution in upload directories; store uploads outside web root; use dedicated file-serving subdomain; re-render images to strip embedded code; limit file size and upload rate.

ov_en: Web cache poisoning exploits discrepancies between what a cache server keys on and the actual response content. By injecting malicious content via unkeyed HTTP headers or parameters, the cache stores a poisoned response delivered to all subsequent users accessing the same URL.
vu_en: Cache poisoning root cause: cache keys typically include only the URL path and a few parameters, while the web application may reflect unkeyed HTTP headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme) into responses. When an attacker injects malicious content via these headers, the cache stores and distributes the poisoned response to all users.
ex_en: Identify caching mechanism (Cache-Control, Age, X-Cache headers), use Param Miner to discover unkeyed headers reflected in responses, craft header values containing malicious JavaScript (e.g., X-Forwarded-Host: evil.com), send request to cache the poisoned response, verify that subsequent clean requests return the poisoned content.
mi_en: Configure cache keys to include all response-influencing parameters and headers; strictly validate and encode HTTP header values reflected in responses; use Vary headers to declare response-affecting headers; avoid caching user-specific content; regularly audit cache configuration and purge suspicious cached entries.

ov_en: HTTP request smuggling (CL-TE type) exploits differing Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding priority between a front-end server (e.g., reverse proxy) and back-end server to smuggle a malicious request inside a normal one, enabling security control bypass, request hijacking, and cache poisoning.
vu_en: HTTP/1.1 spec says Transfer-Encoding takes priority when both CL and TE are present, but implementations differ: the front-end may use Content-Length to determine request boundaries while the back-end uses Transfer-Encoding. This parsing discrepancy causes one front-end request to split into two back-end requests.
ex_en: Use timing techniques to detect CL-TE smuggling; craft requests containing both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked so the front-end forwards one complete request but the back-end parses out a leftover prefix that prepends the next request. Use the smuggled prefix for request hijacking, access control bypass, or stealing other users' request data.
mi_en: Use end-to-end HTTP/2 to eliminate ambiguity; configure front-end to normalize/reject requests with ambiguous headers; configure back-end to reject requests with both CL and TE headers; deploy request smuggling detection rules; use end-to-end encryption to prevent middleware request tampering.

ov_en: Open redirect vulnerabilities allow attackers to redirect users from a trusted domain to an arbitrary external malicious site. Commonly exploited for phishing (leveraging trusted domain reputation), OAuth token theft, and SSRF filter bypass.
vu_en: Applications handling redirect URL parameters (redirect_url, return_to, next, etc.) without strict allowlist validation—performing only simple domain substring checks—can be bypassed via URL encoding, adding subdomains (trusted.com.evil.com), or using @ (trusted.com@evil.com).
ex_en: Identify all redirect parameters in the application, test redirecting to external domains, attempt bypasses if blocked: double URL encoding, protocol-relative URL (//evil.com), @ symbol (https://trusted.com@evil.com), trusted domain as path (https://evil.com/trusted.com), backslash (https://trusted.com\\@evil.com).
mi_en: Strict allowlist validation allowing only predefined trusted domains; use relative paths for on-site redirects; sign redirect URL parameters to prevent tampering; show intermediate confirmation page before redirecting; configure CSP navigate-to to restrict navigable domains.

ov_en: Clickjacking (UI Redressing) is a visual deception attack where an attacker overlays a transparent iframe over a decoy page, tricking users into unknowingly clicking sensitive action buttons hidden in the iframe—potentially triggering account deletion, fund transfers, or authorization grants.
vu_en: The target site lacks X-Frame-Options headers (DENY/SAMEORIGIN) and has no Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive, allowing any third-party page to embed it in an iframe.
ex_en:
1. Detect whether target allows iframe embedding
2. Identify sensitive action pages (delete, transfer, change permissions)
3. Build decoy page with transparent iframe overlay over the target
4. Precisely align target button with decoy button
5. Lure victim to visit and click
mi_en:
1. Set X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN
2. Configure CSP: frame-ancestors 'self'
3. Add confirmation step for sensitive operations
4. Use SameSite Cookie attribute
5. Implement JavaScript frame-busting (as fallback)
